correctness.rationale: The explicit boundary function f_t(e^{iθ})=e^{iθ}exp(it cos2θ) is continuous, unimodular, odd and therefore mean zero. Jacobi–Anger gives Fourier coefficients of S3 f_t at n=−3,−1,1,3 equal −J2(t), iJ1(t), J0(t), iJ1(t). The squared modulus has nonzero frequency lags 0, ±2, ±4, ±6 with |g|² hat(0)=A²+2B²+C², hat(2)=−iBC, hat(4)=B²−AC, hat(6)=−iBC; Parseval gives fourth moment (A²+2B²+C²)^2+4B²C²+2(B²−AC)^2. Independent symbolic expansion from Bessel power series gives 1+5t^6/576−11t^8/2304+473t^10/460800+O(t^12); positive sixth-order coefficient proves an interval of nonzero t with norm>1. At t=1 independently checked the exact rational alternating Bessel interval bound using k=0..9 lower and k=0..10 upper and obtained certified rational lower surplus ≈0.004814465479050505; floating evaluation 1.00481446547905 agrees but is not the proof. Normalized Haar Lp monotonicity extends violation to all p≥4. S3 is a sharp symmetric projector, not the Poisson multiplier; the asserted endpoint conjecture is untouched.
residual_risks: Only operator noncontractivity is established, not sharp S3 norm or minimal frequency cutoff among arbitrary inputs.
Small-t series is local; t=1 uses a separate exact rational certificate; no inference from a finite numerical experiment to all t is made.

originality.rationale: The full primary 13-page Kovalev manuscript was acquired and read, including Proposition 4.1, Remark 4.3, Proposition 4.4 and Conjecture 5.1. It proves L∞ to L3 contractivity of symmetric Fourier sections; Remark 4.3 gives an S1 >3 obstruction using an input with nonzero mean; Proposition 4.4 constructs odd zero-mean data to obstruct Poisson Lp for p>4, but neither evaluates mean-zero S3 at p=4 nor states the sixth-order Bessel fourth-moment failure. The prior published Poisson endpoint-deficit result, read in full, proves a different unimodular family satisfies the finite-radius Poisson p=4 inequality; that does not entail a sharp-cutoff S3 norm. Related one-sided Riesz projection contractivity likewise has a distinct multiplier. Best-of-knowledge O PASS with residual risk of unindexed Fourier-section norm counterexamples; lack of complete priority index does not imply novelty.
residual_risks: A historically unindexed mean-zero sharp Fourier section L4 counterexample may exist under convolution/Dirichlet-kernel terminology; searches are bounded.
No claimed resolution of the Poisson p=4 endpoint; direct Fourier-section obstruction alone cannot rule out cancellations in its positive Abel sum.

value.rationale: A rigorously certified endpoint obstruction for a precise sharp symmetric Fourier section is a motivated counterexample to a natural proof strategy arising from a current harmonic-analysis conjecture. The zero-mean and unimodular restrictions sharply distinguish it from the known S1 example and make the sixth-order loss mathematically informative. No exact operator norm, broader theorem or resolution of the Poisson conjecture is required for this correct natural negative result to be valuable.
residual_risks: The main conjecture may nevertheless hold because a positive Poisson Abel mixture can cancel individual section-level violations.
